title: Campaign donors later paid from the measure's fund
question: Which organizations and firms gave to the campaign for a measure and were later paid from the fund it created or renewed, and how much each way?
finding: 39 donor-and-measure pairs: $1.0 million given, $383.0 million later paid. The largest payee is Charles Pankow Builders, LTD, which gave $2,500 to the campaign for the Public Health and Safety bond and was paid $79.7 million from its fund; the largest gift is Friends of the Urban Forest's $485,000 for the Street tree maintenance fund ($1.5 million paid). A further 19 individual donors, giving $13,220, named an employer that was paid from the fund; they are counted and not listed.
how: Organization and committee donors on the supporting committees' contribution schedules are matched to payees of the measure's fund by name, or through the project's alias table where one organization is paid under another spelling. Amounts given are summed over all supporting committees of the measure; amounts paid are everything the payment file shows, which holds the lines filed under fiscal 2019 to 2027 to date, and the fiscal years shown are the years the payments were issued, read from their voucher numbers. 'Times' is dollars paid for each dollar given.
limits: The same cautions as the measure table. A ratio of thousands of dollars paid for each dollar given describes a service provider's ordinary grant set beside a token contribution, not a return on the contribution. Several payees were funded for the same work before the measure passed. Donor and payee are matched by name; a contribution by a parent, an officer or an affiliate is not matched, and two organizations with the same name would be. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days.
